newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian long bonds limit losses, eye on $A.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian long bonds limit losses, eye on $A.

text.p: *Australian long bonds finish down slightly, but hold above key support levels and outperform Treasuries.
*Curve flattens as short end suffers some late weakness.
Australian bonds finished lower, but losses at the long ended were limited by good support which saw the curve flatten to its lowest level in over two weeks.

Bonds opened testing support after U.S. Treasuries had weakened on Wednesday, but trade volumes were reasonably thin and support held, with bonds moving back to near their previous closes by the midsession.
Long bonds continued to be supported in the afternoon with the spread to U.S. bonds narrowing to 80 points, while short bonds weakened a little, closing right on support at 93.54.
Traders said with little local leads until next week, expectations of favourable December quarter inflation data were adding a supportive tone to the market.
Some partial price indicators for imports and manufacturing released today supported expectations of moderate inflation.
However, despite the expected inflation outcome, some weakness in the Australian dollar may begin to hurt the short end if it is seen weakening the case for a near term rate cut.
In early December, the Australian dollar hit a six-year high above 82 cents, and the dollar's strength was cited by the RBA as a supporting factor behind the December 11 rate cut.

On Thursday, the dollar fell to 5-1/2 month lows, falling to a low of US$0.7702/07 in afternoon trading. A breach of support at US$0.7680 could see the dollar trading down towards US$0.75, currency traders said.

Short end spreads mixed, but long end improves with spreads to U.S. 10-years closing at top of 75-80 points resistance zone. Futures curve closes at its flattest since January 6 as short ends resting on support.
